messages:
devon: Heads up — we're seeing repeated apiserver slow responses and controller-manager restarts in eu-west1 for the last ~15m. GPU node attaches are failing intermittently; provisioner returns 502 and then retries. :eyes:

devon: Quick grep of logs shows a lot of etcd WAL fsync spikes around attach times:
```
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z etcdserver: read WAL fsync duration: 145ms
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z etcdserver: read WAL fsync duration: 812ms
2026-03-20T09:12:04Z etcdserver: read WAL fsync duration: 1200ms
```

sahil: can you paste apiserver error snippets? 502 from which component?

devon: provisioner -> workerpool -> apiserver proxy. apiserver logs show `500 read tcp` and a bunch of `watch` timeouts. snippet:
```
E030 09:12:04.123 api-server request.go:678] Unexpected EOF while reading body
W030 09:12:04.125 cacher: watch handler timed out after 30s
```

maria: iostat on etcd leader node shows nvme await jumping during the window (avg await ~40ms -> spikes >800ms). suspect underlying storage IO contention.

kai: leader election also flipped a few times during the spike (saw 2 leader changes in 3m). that explains controller-manager restarts. leader flips + WAL latency = cascading watcher rebuilds.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0319-947 (priority: high) — paging oncall. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0319-947

irene: short-term mitigations we can do now:
- increase provisioner attach backoff (avoid thundering new attaches)
- mark eu-west1 GPU pool read-only for new allocations and route new jobs to us-east1 fallback pool
- cordon the most IO-noisy etcd replica so leader election picks a healthier disk

sahil: agree. also we should pin heavy compaction/snapshots off the current window. schedule snapshot upload outside peak.

devon: tested cordoning the noisy etcd replica (manual failover); leader moved to node with lower await and watcher queue dropped. attaches started succeeding again for a few minutes, then the burst returned.

maria: ran `iostat -x 1 5` during spike, here's full line that stood out:
```
nvme0n1  8  0.00  0.00  0.00  0.01  0.02  0.05  40.02  800.12
```

kai: we should consider moving etcd leader to an io-optimized instance (nvme provisioned iops) as a near-term fix. long term: separate control-plane storage tier from normal node NVMe pools. cost tradeoff though.

irene: cost note from ops: moving to io-optimized disks for 3 leader replicas ~ +$1.8k/mo. scaling etcd to 5 hosts adds +$3.5k/mo. weighing cheaper mitigations first.

devon: action plan for next 2h:
1) bump provisioner backoff to 20s and enable jitter (irene)
2) cordon and drain the noisy etcd replica, move leader (sahil/devon)
3) add temporary route to fallback us-east1 GPU pool (maria)
4) collect flamegraphs/metrics for WAL fsync and nvme await (kai)

sahil: i'll handle leader move + metrics. devon can update provisioner backoff and rollback if it causes regressions.

maria: routing change to fallback applied — new allocations are going to us-east1 for now. monitoring dashboards updated. :thumbsup:

kai: metrics dashboard shows WAL fsync 95p down from 1.2s -> 120ms after moving leader, but still intermittent spikes. need root cause on disk scheduler or noisy tenant VMs.

irene: creating a tracking ticket for follow-up (postmortem + cost analysis). please drop any logs/graphs there.

devon: nice work all. if spikes continue we'll schedule short maintenance window to repro with fio on candidate node. for now keeping eu-west1 limited for new workloads. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall-bot: Pager cleared (oncall acknowledged).
